Platform/cluster rosters like this are second-order pointers: they enumerate the associations to sweep, and catch industrial-IT suppliers who also sell to financial back offices.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape member index once; use mainly to discover further associations/clusters, not as a primary actor list.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball: IVSZ appeared as a member of this platform in search results
queries_used: IVSZ tagvállalatok lista informatikai szövetség
candidates.observed_blocker: Member-index URL inferred from a member detail URL pattern; treat as unverified

candidates.source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (hu.wikipedia) – history, membership and organisational overview
candidates.why_relevant: Secondary but useful for glossary/alias building and historical continuity (predecessor names, mergers such as the MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék consolidation into MBH). Not authoritative on current membership — use only to normalise names and catch defunct/renamed entities encountered in archives.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch for alias/glossary seeding; do not use as a factual authority on membership.
queries_used: Magyar Bankszövetség tagok listája bankok

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language searches for a concrete ATM operation/maintenance award notice naming a winning bidder ('ATM üzemeltetés eredménytájékoztató nyertes ajánlattevő') returned only generic EKR documentation, training vendors and legal texts — no individual award record.
negative_findings.result_summary: General-purpose web search does not index the interiors of EKR/Értesítő notices well; the notices are inside session-driven search UIs and daily PDF issues.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the collection method must be direct querying of the registers and PDF issues, not web search. Do not conclude such contracts are absent.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian terms 'POS terminál' and 'kártyaszemélyesítés' as free-text queries are dominated by commercial acquirer/SZÉP-kártya marketing pages (OTP, MBH) rather than procurement records.
negative_findings.result_summary: Noisy terms; unusable alone as collection filters.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Flag 'POS terminál', 'bankkártya elfogadás' and 'automata' as noisy — they must be combined with CPV codes or restricted to the procurement domains.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian public-procurement source was found that is specifically scoped to banking/payment technology as a category; the sector is only reachable via CPV codes and keyword filters across general-purpose registers.
negative_findings.result_summary: No vertical/banking-specific procurement portal exists for HU.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's collection design must be filter-driven over general registers; there is no shortcut feed.

negative_findings.description: An EKR public API path was observed in search results (ekr.gov.hu/api/publikus/kozbeszerzesi-hirdetmenyek/{id}/dokumentum-letoltes) but no published API documentation, rate limits or terms-of-use page was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Endpoint pattern plausible; contract and legality of automated use unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A documented API would make this cell cheap and robust; if none exists, plan for headless-browser collection and confirm ToS.

negative_findings.description: The KBA database is served via Oracle APEX with session identifiers embedded in the URL, and the CoRe public search (kereso-core.kozbeszerzes.hu) was not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both recorded as unverified rather than dead; no failed-fetch verdict is claimed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Deep-link-based collection will break; requires session-aware or headless access. Liveness must be settled by the deterministic verification pass.

negative_findings.description: Commercial banks in Hungary are largely private entities and are therefore NOT contracting authorities under Kbt.; their ATM/POS vendor contracts do not appear in these registers at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only state-owned or state-controlled financial actors (MNB, Magyar Államkincstár, Magyar Posta, Diákhitel Központ, state-owned banks) publish.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets a hard ceiling on this cell's coverage of the private banking market; other workstreams must cover commercial-bank vendor relationships.

negative_findings.description: Searches for Hungarian TED notices under CPV 66133000 (processing and clearing services) returned CPV-matching award notices, but the examples surfaced were French rather than Hungarian.
negative_findings.result_summary: Could not evidence a specific Hungarian 66133000 award from search alone; this CPV may be rarely used by Hungarian buyers, who may classify payment work under IT services CPVs instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A CPV-only slice keyed on 66133000 would under-cover Hungary. The CPV set must be widened to IT services (72xxxxxx), software/information systems (488xxxxx) and equipment (30xxxxxx) and verified against the actual TED API rather than a search engine.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian TED notice under CPV 30123600 (cash dispensers / bankjegykiadó automaták) was located via search; results were journalistic coverage of the MNB-mandated ATM rollout instead.
negative_findings.result_summary: ATM procurement in Hungary appears to be driven by commercial banks and a regulator-mandated programme rather than by public tender, so it may be largely absent from TED.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Self-service/ATM competitive intelligence for Hungary probably cannot rely on TED and needs a different workstream (regulator publications, bank disclosures, vendor press).

negative_findings.description: No Hungary-specific EU-level notice was found for CPV 48730000 (security software / HSM) in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The HSM/security-software slice produced no verifiable Hungarian example within this run's search budget.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Security/HSM is a core Printec-adjacent category; absence of evidence here is a search-budget limitation, not proof of absence, and must be re-tested directly against the TED API.

negative_findings.description: The TED bulk-download page, the TED API swagger endpoint, the data.europa.eu TED dataset slug and the EU Knowledge Graph query service for Kohesio were all cited in documentation but not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs recorded from official documentation; liveness and exact paths not confirmed here.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must confirm these before they are wired into a collector; a stale dataset slug would silently produce empty harvests.

negative_findings.description: Searched for Hungarian-language career/job pages for the international payments and self-service vendors most relevant to this market (Printec Hungary, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Worldline, Euronet, Global Payments/SIX). No HU-localised careers URL surfaced for any of them; Printec Hungary Kft. appeared only as a company-registry record (OPTEN), not as a hiring page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor hiring in HU appears to run through global ATS instances and LinkedIn rather than HU career microsites; HU-language vendor career pages could not be confirmed to exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor market-entry signals must therefore be caught in English on global ATS/LinkedIn, and HU-language-only monitoring will systematically miss them.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to surface individual HU job ads that explicitly name a vendor platform (Temenos, Finastra, ACI, Backbase, OpenWay) in a Hungarian bank context. Search returned only vendor corporate/careers pages and generic aggregator pages, no concrete HU ad.
negative_findings.result_summary: Platform-named HU ads were not retrievable from open web search in this pass; they likely exist but are only visible inside board search interfaces and expire quickly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be served by search-engine queries alone — it needs in-board keyword search with scheduled snapshotting, since expired ads vanish from the index.

negative_findings.description: UniCredit Bank Hungary's dedicated HU career page did not surface in the bank career-page enumeration, unlike OTP, MBH, Erste, K&H and Raiffeisen.
negative_findings.result_summary: No UniCredit HU careers URL captured; presumed to route into the UniCredit group careers ATS.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Leaves a named top-tier HU bank uncovered in the employer watchlist.

negative_findings.description: Cvonline.hu is believed to sit in the Alma Career/CV Online group alongside other CEE boards, which would allow cross-border sibling-board monitoring, but this ownership structure was not confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ownership/sibling-board relationship recorded as unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects whether one collection recipe can be reused across CEE boards for regional vendor-entry signals.

negative_findings.description: The cell brief names 'IT Business awards' as a target. I found itbusiness.hu as an active Hungarian enterprise-IT trade magazine covering awards (e.g. Magyar Innovációs Nagydíj 2024), but I did not find a distinct, branded award programme called 'IT Business díj' with its own winners page.
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated IT Business award programme URL located; only editorial coverage of third-party awards.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream collectors should not expect an 'IT Business díj' winners endpoint; the magazine should be treated as trade media (indirect) rather than an award issuer until proven otherwise.

negative_findings.description: For most events I confirmed that sponsor/exhibitor sub-pages EXIST and confirmed their URL patterns (Portfolio /tamogatok; FinTechShow sponsor grades and kiállítók; Sirha /list-of-exhibitors), but I retrieved a full itemised sponsor roster only for Portfolio Banking Technology 2025 (Visa Platinum; OTP Super Gold; Gránit Bank and K&H Gold; unnamed Silver tier).
negative_findings.result_summary: Sponsor page structure confirmed; full company-level rosters largely not yet extracted in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The named URLs are collection targets, not yet collected data; the actual sponsor/exhibitor company lists must be harvested by the collection pass before any actor-map conclusions are drawn.

negative_findings.description: I searched in Hungarian for a Magyar Bankszövetség-run 'Bankkártya Fórum' and for a dedicated Hungarian banking-cards forum under the association; no such standing event page surfaced. Card/payment-specific events in Hungary appear to be run by commercial organisers (IIR Hungary Kártyapiac, businessevents.hu Digital Payment, FinTechZone PayTechShow) rather than by the association.
negative_findings.result_summary: Association-run card forum not located; commercial organisers hold that niche.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Redirects collection effort away from bankszovetseg.hu for card/POS vendor mapping and toward the commercial organisers, which is where sponsor tiers are actually published.

negative_findings.description: I did not run local-language searches for cash-handling / ATM / cash-logistics events (e.g. 'készpénzlogisztika konferencia', 'bankjegy konferencia', 'ATM konferencia Magyarország'), which are directly relevant to a hardware/self-service vendor's view of the Hungarian market.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search space not covered in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A significant slice of the relevant event landscape (cash handling, ATM/self-service, branch automation) may be undiscovered.

negative_findings.description: Generic event aggregators (conferenceindex.org, paytech.events, fintechweekly.com meetup pages, luma.com listings) surface Hungary entries but frequently list stale, cancelled or predatory events, and Luma pages are JS-rendered so plain fetching may return an empty shell.
negative_findings.result_summary: Aggregators usable as lead lists only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents the collection pipeline from ingesting phantom events as real market signals.

negative_findings.description: No free, machine-readable bulk/open-data export of the Hungarian company register or of the annual-accounts corpus was found. The Ministry of Justice explicitly sells the beszámoló dataset ('Beszámoló állomány értékesítése'), and KSH's statisztikai számjel tool appears to support single-entity lookups only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk access exists but is commercial/licensed (Céginformációs Szolgálat, Opten, D&B); no data.gov-style free dump surfaced in either hu or en searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any systematic HU vendor-population screen requires a budget line or a licence negotiation; planning around 'free bulk scraping' would be both legally risky and technically unsupported.

negative_findings.description: No documented public API for e-cégjegyzék, e-beszámoló or Cégközlöny was located in this pass; commercial providers (Opten, D&B) are the likely API route but their endpoint documentation was not surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only human-facing web query forms found for the statutory portals.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume form-driven, rate-limited retrieval or a commercial feed, not a clean official API.

negative_findings.description: Searches did not surface Hungarian legal entities for Worldline or Nexi under those names in the aggregator layer, whereas Diebold Nixdorf Kft. and NCR Magyarország Kft. resolved immediately.
negative_findings.result_summary: Absent from search results only — this is not evidence of absence: these groups commonly operate in HU via differently named legal entities, via a branch (fióktelep), or cross-border from another EU country.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor entity resolution in HU cannot rely on brand names; it needs alias/legacy-name handling (e.g. Wincor Nixdorf → Diebold Nixdorf, Bisnode → Dun & Bradstreet Hungary) and BRIS cross-border lookups.

negative_findings.description: The central beneficial-ownership register (TTNY, AFAD Act) is not publicly queryable; access is limited to authorities, supervisors and obliged service providers via AFADREG registration.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public information pages exist (NAV, MKVK, legal commentary) but the data itself is out of reach for market research.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Ultimate-owner questions must be answered from cégkivonat ownership entries, filed company documents, or licensed commercial family-tree data — not from the UBO register.

negative_findings.description: The register/filings layer covers vendors and competitors well but serves 'partnerships' and 'case studies' only indirectly.
negative_findings.result_summary: Ownership links, joint-venture entities and consortium companies are visible; commercial partnerships and bank reference cases are not, except occasionally in the kiegészítő melléklet or üzleti jelentés narrative.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This cell should not be expected to deliver partnership/case-study evidence; those belong to procurement, press and vendor-website cells.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian public source was found in this pass that identifies the hardware or software supplier behind the self-checkout estates of Tesco HU, Lidl HU or SPAR HU. Retailer press and trade media report unit counts and customer attitudes, never the vendor.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple hu-language searches on 'önkiszolgáló kassza bevezetés szállító' returned chain-vs-chain unit counts (Tesco ~1028, SPAR ~900, Lidl ~1300 reported 2025) and legislative debate, but no supplier attribution.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The largest single block of non-bank self-service demand in Hungary is vendor-opaque; competitive share for SCO hardware in HU cannot be inferred from open sources alone and will need registry filings, integrator references or trade-fair material.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Hungarian vending / self-service machine industry association website was identified in this pass (searched alongside OKSZ). Only the general retail association OKSZ was confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Association-oriented hu query returned OKSZ and trade press only; no 'Magyar Vending Szövetség'-type body surfaced in results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: An unattended-retail association would be a high-value pointer to operators, suppliers and market sizing for cash-handling and vending payment; its absence from results is a coverage hole rather than proof of non-existence.

negative_findings.description: Hospital-sector self-service and payment kiosks (betegirányító kioszk, kórházi fizetőautomata, parkolás kórházi területen) produced no usable Hungarian hits in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The combined parking/hospital query returned only municipal parking material; the search explicitly returned nothing on hospital payment automats.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Healthcare is named in the cell definition; it is currently uncovered, and hospital procurement is exactly the kind of activity that would sit in EKR rather than the press.

negative_findings.description: Utilities (MVM, water and district-heating providers) as buyers of bill-payment kiosks / befizetőautomaták were not covered by a dedicated search in this pass, so no utility-specific source is recorded.
negative_findings.result_summary: No query was run on 'MVM ügyfélszolgálat befizetőautomata' or equivalent within this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Utility customer-service points are a classic cash-in/kiosk buyer segment; leaving it unsearched understates non-bank payment-acceptance demand.

negative_findings.description: None of the listed URLs were liveness-verified by this agent; several (EKR search pages, MNV szerződéskereső, NAV list-file endpoint) are dynamic or parameterised and may behave differently to an automated fetcher.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sources were recorded from search-result metadata and result snippets; no fetch verdicts are asserted.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must treat any 403/timeout on nav.gov.hu, ekr.gov.hu or mnv.hu as bot-defence, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: Neither the national supported-project search nor Kohesio offers a filter for 'financial sector' or 'payments'; the national search filters are programme, year, OP, call title, applicant name, fund and geography only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector targeting must be done by keyword on project titles/descriptions and by applicant-name lists of known banks, savings institutions, fintechs and POS/payment vendors, or via NACE codes on the state-aid side.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must include a curated actor list and a Hungarian keyword lexicon rather than relying on a sector facet; recall will otherwise be poor.

negative_findings.description: Grant registers publish the beneficiary, not the supplier that implements the project. No source found in this cell exposes the implementing IT vendor for a privately funded grant project.
negative_findings.result_summary: Supplier identification requires joining grant records to public procurement (EKR/TED/Közbeszerzési Értesítő) for public beneficiaries, or to vendor case studies/press for private ones.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cell #15 alone cannot answer 'who supplied it' for private beneficiaries; the workstream needs an explicit join step with the procurement cells.

negative_findings.description: No documented open API or bulk download endpoint was found for the palyazat.gov.hu supported-project search; only an in-page Export control was observed and its formats were not stated.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treat bulk extraction as unresolved; an XHR/JSON endpoint may exist behind the search UI but was not confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects feasibility and cost of systematic monitoring of the single most important source in this cell.

negative_findings.description: Searches did not surface a Hungarian national state-aid transparency portal separate from the Commission's TAM; secondary commentary indicates Hungary reports through TAM while some other Member States use domestic sites.
negative_findings.result_summary: This is unverified secondary commentary, not a confirmed fact about Hungary's reporting channel.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If a domestic Hungarian aid register (e.g. under the Támogatásokat Vizsgáló Iroda) exists, it would be an additional high-value source; needs a dedicated hu-language check.

negative_findings.description: Several local terms are noisy: 'DIMOP pályázat' and 'GINOP pályázat' return overwhelmingly SEO/consultancy marketing pages; 'digitalizáció' alone returns generic SME IT content unrelated to financial infrastructure; 'fizetés' collides with 'salary/payment of wages'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query design should combine programme codes with financial terms (bank, hitelintézet, pénzforgalom, kártyaelfogadás, POS, terminál, számlavezetés) and exclude consultancy domains.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents precision collapse in automated collection.

negative_findings.description: None of the international trade titles in this cell (Finextra, The Paypers, PYMNTS, IBSi, Retail Banker International, FinTech Futures) appears to operate a Hungary-specific section or correspondent; Hungary coverage is event-driven and sparse, surfacing only when a large vendor issues a press release.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungary appears as a keyword tag (FinTech Futures) or as scattered articles, not as a maintained beat. Coverage clusters heavily on OTP Bank and Erste Bank Hungary, with almost nothing on mid-tier banks, savings cooperatives or merchant acquirers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This cell will under-report the Hungarian market by construction; it must be paired with Hungarian-language domestic media and MNB/regulatory filings rather than treated as a standalone view.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language search was run as required, but by definition this cell covers English-language international outlets; the Hungarian query surfaced only domestic sources (MNB fintech and digitalisation report, Portfolio.hu, FinTechZone, Magyar Bankszövetség press releases) that belong to other coverage cells, not international trade/analyst coverage.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query 'magyar bank nemzetközi sajtó megállapodás technológiai szolgáltató fizetési piac elemzés' returned mnb.hu, portfolio.hu, bankszovetseg.hu, fintechzone.hu — all domestic. No Hungarian-language edition or Hungarian mirror of Finextra/The Paypers/PYMNTS/IBSi was found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms there is no Hungarian-language on-ramp into the international trade titles; local-language monitoring cannot substitute for, and is not duplicated by, this cell.

negative_findings.description: No freely accessible analyst source was found that gives Hungarian market share by payments vendor or acquirer (terminal estate share, processing share, core-banking installed base).
negative_findings.result_summary: GlobalData, Euromonitor and Mordor abstracts give market sizing and, in Mordor's case, a vendor roster, but no share splits without purchase. IBSi's Sales League Table is paid and not Hungary-segmented in public view.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Competitive-position questions cannot be answered from this cell without a licensed purchase; expectations and budget should be set accordingly.

negative_findings.description: ITKeyMedia and Emerging Europe were probed as possible additional English-language CEE outlets covering Hungarian banking technology; neither returned Hungary payments/banking coverage in the results obtained.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned The Recursive, Finovate and FinTech Futures instead; no ITKeyMedia result appeared at all.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These should be re-probed directly on their own site search before being written off — a single search miss is not evidence of absence.

negative_findings.description: No MNB register or publication was found that names the technology suppliers (POS terminal vendors, switch/processing software, HSM, terminal management) used by Hungarian PSPs. Registers enumerate legal entities and licence scopes, not their IT supply chain.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on AFR technology supplier terms returned MNB programme pages and press coverage, but no supplier-level register field.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The A6 vendor-mapping objective cannot be satisfied from MNB registers alone; supplier identity must be inferred from procurement portals (EKR/TED), outsourcing notifications, or vendor press releases.

negative_findings.description: MNB Payment Systems Reports and payment statistics publish aggregate acquirer-side metrics (acceptance points, POS terminals, transaction values) but I did not find a published table attributing market share to named acquirers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Report excerpts describe market-level growth (e.g. online acceptance points +20.7%, physical -2%) without per-acquirer breakdown.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Competitor ranking on the acquiring side will need the Aranykönyv institution-level data or commercial sources rather than the payment statistics set.

negative_findings.description: I did not establish whether intezmenykereso.mnb.hu or the open-banking TPP pages expose a downloadable CSV/JSON or an API; only the HTML search UI was observed via search results and a hub-page fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: No API documentation surfaced in either hu or en searches.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design (scrape vs API) is unresolved; a technical probe of the register endpoints is needed before building a collector.

negative_findings.description: The pénzforgalmi táblakészlet archive URL sits under mnb.hu/archivum/, which suggests content has been migrated to statisztika.mnb.hu. I did not fetch it, so its current status is unknown.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search index still returns the archivum path; hypothesis is that it redirects or is a frozen archive, not that it is dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical time series may need to be sourced from the new statistics portal instead.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian systemic bank appears to publish a supplier/vendor register, procurement page or tender portal on its own site. Searches combining bank names with 'beszállító', 'szállító', 'közbeszerzés', 'pályázat' returned factoring products (MBH Beszállítói Faktoring) rather than procurement disclosures.
negative_findings.result_summary: The term 'beszállítói' in HU banking web content overwhelmingly denotes supply-chain-finance products, not the bank's own suppliers — a strong false-friend term for this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: vendor identity must be reconstructed from voluntary announcements, annual-report outsourcing notes and vendor-side claims, not from any procurement disclosure.

negative_findings.description: Bank name queries in Hungarian are dominated by consumer-facing aggregator/tabloid coverage (penzcentrum.hu, promotions.hu, index.hu tag pages) about fees, outages and warnings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Generic queries like 'K&H bank hírek' surface consumer news noise; precision requires pairing the bank name with terms such as 'bevezetés', 'rendszer', 'együttműködés', 'partner', 'kiszervezés'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection queries must be term-constrained or the pipeline will be flooded with irrelevant retail-banking noise.

negative_findings.description: The MBH extraordinary-disclosure page slug could not be confirmed to a single canonical form; the search snippet showed a URL that may be a truncated or altered variant.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with a caveat rather than asserting reachability; no fetch was performed to confirm.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A deterministic verification pass must resolve the real slug from the /befektetoi hub before scheduling collection, or the source will look dead when it is not.

negative_findings.description: No K&H Bank vendor/core-banking supplier announcement was found in either language during this pass; K&H (KBC group) appears to communicate technology changes mainly as product launches and maintenance notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: K&H technology-supplier identification will likely require the indirect route (maintenance notices, KBC group reports, conference speaker lists) rather than a press release.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for coverage of one of the eight target banks and justifies prioritising indirect sources for it.

negative_findings.description: Gránit Bank does not appear to run a page labelled 'sajtószoba'; its public communication seems routed through the 'Befektetőknek' investor section and BÉT filings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searching 'granitbank.hu sajtószoba' returned the investor page and third-party company registries instead of a press room.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for Gránit must target the IR/BÉT path, not a press-room crawler template reused from the other seven banks.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language Visa Hungary newsroom or country press page was surfaced by local-language searching; Visa's Hungarian announcements appear to reach the market only via the pan-European newsroom and Hungarian trade press pickup.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on 'Mastercard Visa Magyarország ... bejelentés' returned Mastercard European newsroom, HU trade press and the Év Bankja programme, but no Visa HU country site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Visa-side partnership and certification signals for Hungary will have to be reconstructed indirectly (bank press releases, trade media, Visa global registry), creating an asymmetry versus Mastercard coverage.

negative_findings.description: Mastercard's actual certified-vendor listing (GVCP) and the Digital Vendor Directory sit behind Mastercard Connect customer login; only the programme FAQ is openly published.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public FAQ PDF found and readable; the vendor list itself is stated to live on the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most authoritative directory of who may personalise Mastercard cards for Hungarian issuers is not openly collectable; membership must be inferred from vendor claims and issuer announcements.

negative_findings.description: KELER's public-interest data page marks the közbeszerzés (public procurement) section as 'Nem áll rendelkezésre' — no procurement procedures reported — and several payment/subsidy sections as unavailable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the 'közzéteendő szerződések' route remains for KELER vendor discovery; the Kbt. procurement gazette will not cover KELER.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor discovery for the CSD depends on a single disclosure artefact whose completeness cannot be cross-checked against procurement notices.

negative_findings.description: The KELER contract-register file URL (kelerms2024.sensenet.com/api/Content/File?id=198638) was obtained from a search index, not fetched by me; its id-based form suggests instability.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with reduced confidence; not asserted as live.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector hardcoding this id would silently break; the link must be resolved dynamically from keler.hu.

negative_findings.description: No public, named disclosure was found of the technology vendor(s) behind the GIROInstant/AFR core instant-payment platform itself (the switching engine), as distinct from peripheral IT suppliers listed in GIRO's contract register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language searches on 'GIROInstant platform szállító / technológiai partner' returned scheme and adoption content, not a platform-vendor attribution.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most strategically important vendor fact in this cell is not directly published; it must be triangulated from the contract register, job adverts and MNB documentation.

negative_findings.description: Repeated Hungarian-language searches for a Barion press room / newsroom ('Barion sajtószoba', 'Barion Payment Zrt hírek sajtó') returned only integration tutorials, reseller pages and company-registry entries — no Barion-operated press-release index surfaced in search results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Barion's own announcement channel could not be pinned to a specific URL; PR appears to reach the market via Prim.hu, Portfolio.hu and FinTechZone instead. Not evidence the page does not exist — only that it is not search-discoverable from these queries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Barion is one of the two most important independent HU PSPs; without a primary announcement feed, partnership signals must be picked up second-hand with a lag and lower fidelity.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian-language Revolut or Wise press room surfaced. Revolut HU branch news (MNB registration late 2025, migration of 2M+ clients, qvik and payment-request rollout, new transaction fees) was found only through Hungarian financial media (Portfolio, Világgazdaság, HVG, Economx, Infostart, Bank360, Biztosdöntés).
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage is media-mediated rather than issuer-primary for the neobank actors in this cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Neobank moves into local rails (qvik, HUF accounts) directly reshape acceptance and merchant payment behaviour; a media-only pipeline risks missing technical/partner detail that press releases carry.

negative_findings.description: Searched explicitly for a Nexi-Euronet Hungarian ATM/POS acquiring partnership announcement; nothing of the kind was found. Both operate in Hungary independently.
negative_findings.result_summary: No such partnership evidenced. Recorded as a negative finding rather than inferred.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a fabricated linkage entering the actor map.

negative_findings.description: For Wise's Hungarian presence, no Hungarian-language corporate or regulatory terminology beyond the generic 'fióktelep' surfaced; the only concrete artefact was a Hungarian branch registration reference and Wise's own hu-locale marketing blog (wise.com/hu/blog) which writes about competitors (PayU) rather than about Wise's HU partnerships.
negative_findings.result_summary: Wise HU is under-covered in this pass; local-language terminology for its acquiring/merchant activity may not exist because it has little merchant-acceptance footprint in HU.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Wise was named in the cell scope; its absence from acceptance-side sources may itself be the finding, but should be confirmed rather than assumed.

negative_findings.description: Portfolio.hu and Világgazdaság articles on Revolut/acquiring are partially paywalled; MNB Intézménykereső and GIRO's document library are behind query/filter UIs rather than static listings.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several of the highest-value sources need either metadata-only collection or form-driven fetching rather than simple crawling.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must budget for form interaction and for licence-safe metadata-only ingestion of paywalled press.

negative_findings.description: No Diebold Nixdorf case study or success story naming a Hungarian bank was located across the DN case-study hubs and search. Visible European entries were Valiant, FOREX, Sparkasse Hannover, CSOB and similar.
negative_findings.result_summary: DN publishes an extensive named-client library, but no HU client surfaced in this pass. Absence is unconfirmed, not proven — the library is paginated and partly PDF-only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: DN is a prime ATM/self-service competitor in HU (it maintains a Hungarian legal entity with Budapest and Székesfehérvár sites), so the lack of a public HU reference means its HU install base must be inferred from registry, tender and job-posting signals instead.

negative_findings.description: No Temenos press release or success story naming a Hungarian bank was found, despite targeted queries against the Temenos press and success-story indexes and against named HU candidates (Gránit, MagNet, Erste).
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic Temenos market/analyst releases surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests Temenos may have little or no publicly disclosed Hungarian core-banking footprint; if the Hungarian core-banking layer is served by local/regional players instead, the competitor map for A6 must shift toward local vendors.

negative_findings.description: No Ingenico, Verifone or PAX customer reference, partner page or press release naming a Hungarian bank, acquirer or PSP was found. Results returned only generic terminal-market comparisons and US reseller shops.
negative_findings.result_summary: POS terminal vendors do not appear to publish HU-named references in indexed English content; no Hungarian-language equivalent surfaced either.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal-supplier mapping in HU cannot rely on vendor case studies and will need acquirer disclosures, certification lists, tender records and MNB/terminal-fleet statistics instead.

negative_findings.description: No INETCO customer reference, case study or press release naming a Hungarian institution was found, and no Thales payShield case study naming a Hungarian bank was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic product and FAQ pages returned for Thales; nothing HU-specific for INETCO.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Transaction-monitoring and HSM suppliers to HU banks stay invisible in vendor marketing; these relationships will have to be inferred from job ads, integrator partner lists and certification/compliance disclosures.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries using esettanulmány / referencia / szállító / rendszerbevezetés / sajtóközlemény returned regulator, banking-association and consultancy content rather than international-vendor case studies. International vendors appear not to publish Hungarian-language customer references at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: The productive Hungarian-language route was not vendor marketing but local integrators (Capsys, T-Systems Magyarország), local trade press (itbusiness.hu) and company registries.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that for cell #7 the local-language layer works as a corroboration and snowballing channel, not as a primary source of vendor case studies.

negative_findings.description: The Finastra release covers Raiffeisen Bank's core retail services across its markets; whether Hungary is explicitly enumerated inside the release body was not verified in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a high-value lead requiring full-text verification, not as a confirmed HU supplier fact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Group-level vendor announcements are routinely over-read as country-level facts; the HU claim must be confirmed against the release text or the local subsidiary before use.

negative_findings.description: No public, itemised bank-client reference list was found for 4iG, Grepton or Sysdata PSE. Searches in Hungarian returned only generic capability language ('pénzügyi szektor', 'rendszerintegráció') without named bank accounts.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sector positioning confirmed; specific bank names not disclosed on public marketing pages in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Account-level attribution for these integrators will have to come from procurement notices, annual-report customer-concentration notes, job ads and press coverage rather than vendor reference pages.

negative_findings.description: No IBM Hungary press announcement naming a Hungarian bank client (OTP, K&H) for a core-banking or infrastructure project surfaced in en-language search; the OTP core selection that did surface is with Intellect/iGCB, not IBM.
negative_findings.result_summary: IBM Hungary's bank-facing footprint remains unquantified from public search alone.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: IBM Hungary is in the cell's actor list but currently has no verified public evidence base; treat its competitive weight as unknown rather than assumed.

negative_findings.description: 'Sysdata' is ambiguous in Hungary: results resolve to Sysdata PSE Kft. (software engineering, since 1991) rather than a 'Sysdata Zrt.'. 'Docler' likewise did not resolve to any banking-IT entity; the relevant local ISV in the wealth/securities space is Dorsum Zrt.
negative_findings.result_summary: Actor list needs correction: Sysdata PSE Kft. and Dorsum Zrt. are the real entities; 'Docler' appears to be a mis-specification.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Querying wrong legal names produces false negatives and wasted crawl budget; entity resolution against the company registry should precede collection.

negative_findings.description: The CARDNET corporate homepage (https://www.cardnet.hu/) was inferred from the company name and third-party profiles; it was not fetched in this pass, and no direct-fetch verification was performed on any URL in this slice.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded with reduced confidence pending the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a plausible-but-wrong domain from entering the source register as verified.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian trade-press outlet was found that maintains a structured, machine-readable index of bank IT contracts/vendor wins. Deal detail is scattered across narrative articles with no tagging convention for 'szállító' or 'beszállító' in the banking context (only Piac & Profit exposes a generic supplier tag).
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches combining Hungarian outlet names with 'szerződés', 'szállító', 'beszállító' returned mostly public-procurement PDFs (NAV, NISZ, kozbeszerzes.hu) rather than press indexes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection from this cell must be keyword/NER-driven over full article streams; a tag-following strategy will under-collect badly.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language queries naming a specific outlet frequently returned public-procurement documents and Wikipedia rather than that outlet's own articles, indicating the search index poorly covers deep archives of Bitport, HWSW, ITBusiness and vg.hu.
negative_findings.result_summary: e.g. the 'Portfolio.hu ... szállító szerződés' query surfaced kozbeszerzes.hu and nisz.hu PDFs above any Portfolio article.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: External search engines cannot be relied on to enumerate this cell; on-site search endpoints and RSS must be used directly.

negative_findings.description: Computerworld.hu (the historically dominant Hungarian enterprise-IT title) could not be confirmed as an active, currently published outlet in this pass; no live article was surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Query naming computerworld.hu returned only SG.hu and Prim.hu results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If it is defunct, its archive may still be a valuable historical record of bank IT deals and should be sought via web archives rather than a live crawl.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian press reporting was found on 2025-era ATM/self-service hardware or managed-service supplier contracts naming vendors such as Diebold Nixdorf or NCR/Atleos; only Euronet's own commercial pages and the MNB ATM-deployment regulation surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Coverage of the ATM mandate is regulatory and consumer-facing, not procurement-facing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For cash-automation vendor intelligence this cell is weak; the ATM obligation-transfer contracts between banks (due July 2025 per the MNB rule) are more likely to appear in regulatory/legal sources than in trade press.

negative_findings.description: A large share of the highest-yield Hungarian bank-technology content (FinTechZone, ITBusiness ICT-market section, Prim.hu, Forbes brand-club) is sponsored or PR-derived rather than independently reported.
negative_findings.result_summary: FinTechZone is published by FinTech Group Kft., an agency whose stated business is positioning technology suppliers to the financial sector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor claims from these outlets must be recorded as claims, not facts; credibility scoring must be applied per-item, not per-outlet.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for a standalone Hungarian bank-card / payments professional association ('Magyar Bankkártya Szakmai Szövetség', 'kártyaszövetség tagjai'). No such independent association surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card-industry coordination in Hungary appears to sit INSIDE the Magyar Bankszövetség as its 'Bankkártya munkacsoport' and the 'Pénzforgalmi (PAD) + SEPA munkacsoport', not in a separate legal association. Card-scheme presence (Mastercard, Visa) is instead visible via Hungarian Fintech Association and DKSZ membership.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids a wasted recurring crawl target and redirects payments-specific association monitoring to the Bankszövetség working-group pages, which are the real locus.

negative_findings.description: Ecommerce Hungary (ecommerce.hu) and Digitális Kereskedelmi Szövetség (dksz.hu) homepages were fetched looking for a 'tagjaink'/'tagok' directory page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Neither exposes a structured member directory from the homepage. Ecommerce Hungary describes member CATEGORIES (banks, payment providers such as Barion and Cofidis, logistics, ERP/CRM/BI integrators) and gives a contact email instead; DKSZ shows only board portraits and named partners (Mastercard, Google, DHL Express, PwC, IVSZ, Growww Digital, Boxy, Oander).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Actor extraction for the merchant/e-commerce payments side must fall back to logo walls, event sponsor pages and press releases rather than a clean roster scrape — higher extraction cost and lower recall.

negative_findings.description: Inspected the IVSZ member directory (ivsz.hu/tagok) for fintech/banking-IT identification.
negative_findings.result_summary: The directory's filters are by company SIZE (Mikro/KKV/Nagyvállalati/Multi/Társult) and by broad tagozat (Informatikai, Digitális, Startup és Scale-up, Telekommunikációs) — there is no financial-services or fintech facet. The first pages show general enterprise IT firms (4D Soft, 4iG, Abesse, ARCANUM Development) with no vertical marker.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Full pagination plus per-company enrichment (website/TEÁOR/reference-customer check) is required to isolate banking-relevant suppliers; a filter-only harvest would return mostly noise.

negative_findings.description: Searched hu for the Magyar Fintech Szövetség (MAFISZ/HFA) member registry.
negative_findings.result_summary: Open-web search largely returns the 2020 founding-member set (Bankmonitor, Barion, BÁV Faktor, Blueopes, Flexibill, Péntech, Rocketsheperd, TechTeamer, Tőkeportál). The current, much larger roster (~50+, incl. Revolut, Mastercard, Visa, Dorsum, Finshape, BÉT) is only visible by fetching hunfintech.com/hu/tagok directly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Search-engine-mediated collection would materially under-count and date-skew the fintech actor map; direct directory fetch must be the primary method for this association.

negative_findings.description: The MKIK national chamber registry KNYR (https://knyr.mkik.hu/Kamreg/Nyilvantarto/Kereses) and the inferred IPAR 4.0 member index (https://i40platform.hu/hu/szervezet/tagok/) were identified via search snippets and URL-pattern inference, not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Both URLs are recorded with confidence below that of directly fetched pages. KNYR is a query-form application, so a plain GET may not return content even when the service is healthy.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream liveness verification should not mark these dead on a single non-200/empty response; they need form-aware or browser-based checking.

negative_findings.description: Looked for a Hungarian-language umbrella term or association covering 'payment service providers' / acquirers as a membership body distinct from banks.
negative_findings.result_summary: No dedicated 'pénzforgalmi szolgáltatók szövetsége' style body was found. PSPs appear scattered across the Fintech Association, Ecommerce Hungary and IVSZ. The only sector-wide enumeration of payment service providers appears to be regulator-side (MNB registers), which falls outside this association/chamber cell.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms there is no association-based shortcut to a complete PSP/acquirer list in Hungary; that enumeration must be sourced from the regulator cell instead, and this cell should not be asked to close that gap.

coverage_gaps.description: No complete enumerated list yet of Hungarian state-owned or state-controlled financial-sector contracting authorities (beyond MNB, Magyar Államkincstár, Magyar Posta, Diákhitel Központ, MÁV) whose own disclosure pages should be monitored.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the 'Nyilvántartott ajánlatkérők' (registered contracting authorities) register on kozbeszerzes.hu and filter by financial/postal/transport activity to build the buyer roster.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact CPV code set for banking/payment technology in HU procurement is not yet fixed. Only CPV 30144200 (jegykiadó gépek) was confirmed by name; codes for ATMs, cash-handling, card personalisation and self-service kiosks remain to be pinned down.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the free CPV lists (khf.hu PDF, tender-ertesito.hu list) and reconcile against the official EU CPV vocabulary to build an authoritative filter set before any bulk collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor names in HU notices appear in inconsistent legal forms (Zrt./Kft./Nyrt., accented vs unaccented, Hungarian subsidiary vs group brand), which will fragment award counts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan a normalisation step keyed on tax number/company registry number where notices carry it; consider Opentender's already-normalised supplier field as a cross-check.

coverage_gaps.description: Framework-agreement call-offs under the KEF centralised system may not generate individual public award notices, hiding the actual vendor-buyer pair for central-government payment/IT purchases.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate whether KEF publishes call-off/consumption data or supplier catalogues publicly; if not, log as a structural blind spot and rely on the framework roster plus annual KEF reporting.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed Hungarian term set yet for 'card personalisation' and 'self-service banking kiosk' as they are actually written in procurement notices; the seed term 'kártyaszemélyesítés' returned no procurement hits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Mine confirmed notice PDFs for the in-use phrasing (e.g. kártyagyártás, kártyaperszonalizáció, ügyfélhívó/önkiszolgáló terminál, bankjegykiadó automata, készpénzbefizető automata) and rebuild the glossary from observed text rather than from translation.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth is unassessed: EKR only became mandatory from 2018, so pre-2018 awards live in older Értesítő archives with a different structure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Determine the earliest machine-readable year in each register and decide the backfill horizon needed for rebid-cycle analysis (typically 8-10 years for ATM fleet contracts).

coverage_gaps.description: The mapping from banking/payments subject matter to actual CPV codes used by Hungarian buyers has not been empirically validated — it is currently an assumption.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a TED API frequency analysis: all HU notices for the last 5 years, count CPV codes among notices whose title/description matches a HU/EN payments-and-banking keyword list, and derive the CPV slice from the data instead of a priori.

coverage_gaps.description: TED and EU-funded award databases cover public buyers. Commercial Hungarian banks (OTP, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, MBH, UniCredit, CIB) procure payments technology privately and appear only when state-owned or EU-cofunded.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Flag to the coordinating agent that private-bank vendor intelligence needs a different cell (vendor press releases, bank annual reports, MNB publications); do not treat TED coverage as market coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian supplier names in TED/EKR appear with varying legal-form suffixes (Kft., Zrt., Nyrt., Bt.), accents and consortium constructions; no normalisation or tax-number join has been designed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a HU entity-normalisation step keyed on adószám/cégjegyzékszám where present, and reuse Opentender's entity-matching output as a starting dictionary.

coverage_gaps.description: Much Hungarian public IT buying runs through central purchasing bodies and framework agreements (központosított közbeszerzés, keretmegállapodás), where the TED award names the framework holder and the real call-offs are invisible.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify the Hungarian central purchasing body's framework registers and call-off reporting, and treat framework awards as pointers to be resolved rather than as final contract values.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian national portals migrate content (archive.palyazat.gov.hu already exists as a separate archive host), so links captured today may move.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot every harvested Hungarian notice/project record locally at collection time and store the retrieval date; do not rely on live national URLs for provenance.

coverage_gaps.description: Job ads are the most perishable source class in this run: HU board ads typically expire in 30-60 days and are then removed from both the board and the search index, so any signal not captured within the window is lost permanently.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a weekly snapshot-and-diff collector over the watchlist (profession.hu keyword searches, each bank/GIRO/MNB ATS, vendor ATS country filters) with full-text archiving of ad bodies, not just titles.

coverage_gaps.description: The two highest-yield sources for vendor-side signals (LinkedIn Jobs, Glassdoor) are auth-walled and ToS-restricted, so they cannot be part of an automated pipeline.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Designate them as analyst-manual sources with a fixed weekly checklist of watchlist companies, or evaluate a licensed jobs-data provider for compliant coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Employer watchlist currently covers large banks, GIRO, MNB and a few HU software firms. Missing: UniCredit HU, CIB, Gránit, MagNet, MBH Fintechlab, Takarék entities, MFB, plus HU-based card processors, ATM independent deployers (Euronet HU), acquirers and PSPs, and the bank IT captives (e.g. Deutsche Telekom/IT Services Hungary, Diebold/NCR service partners).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the watchlist using bankweb.hu's banki-állás directory and the MNB register of payment institutions, then attach each entity's career URL.

coverage_gaps.description: A stable HU keyword set for banking/payments job ads is only partially established (core banki rendszer, rendszerszervező, integrációs fejlesztő, POS terminál, ATM üzemeltetés, pénzforgalom, kártyarendszer, azonnali fizetés/AFR, qvik). Noisy terms not yet flagged: 'bank' matches non-financial employers, 'terminál' matches logistics, 'core' matches unrelated English-in-HU usage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and version a HU/EN keyword file with precision weights and negative keywords before automating collection; validate recall against a hand-labelled sample of 50 ads.

coverage_gaps.description: No baseline exists for normal hiring volume per employer, so a spike (the actual weak signal) cannot yet be distinguished from routine churn or seasonal recruitment.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Collect at least two quarters of per-employer ad counts before drawing programme-level inferences; store counts as a time series alongside ad text.

coverage_gaps.description: No source yet covering ATM / cash logistics / branch self-service events and their exhibitor lists in Hungary.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run hu searches: 'készpénzlogisztika konferencia', 'ATM üzemeltetés konferencia Magyarország', 'bankfiók automatizálás konferencia', 'önkiszolgáló bankolás szakmai nap'; also check MNB készpénz-related professional days.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one trade-fair exhibitor directory (Sirha Budapest) captured. Retail-technology and merchant-facing fairs where POS/payment acceptance vendors exhibit are otherwise unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the HUNGEXPO event calendar (hungexpo.hu/events/) and identify every fair with a kiállítói lista containing payment/POS/pénztárgép categories; add each directory as its own source.

coverage_gaps.description: Sponsor rosters were confirmed only for recent editions; the multi-year time series that would show vendor entry, exit and tier escalation has not been assembled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Backfill Portfolio event ids (593, 873, 1017, 1401, 1496, 1671, 1831) and FinTechShow editions from 2019 onward; supplement with web.archive.org captures where pages have been retired.

coverage_gaps.description: International award programmes that rank Hungarian banks (Global Finance, Euromoney, The Banker country awards, Mastercard/Visa regional awards) were not searched, though they are frequently cited by Hungarian banks in their own PR.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search in en for 'Global Finance best bank Hungary', 'Euromoney awards for excellence Hungary', 'The Banker bank of the year Hungary' and register the award pages as direct sources.

coverage_gaps.description: The highest-value signal in this cell — a bank executive and a named supplier co-presenting a case study — requires parsing speaker affiliation pairs per session, which no source publishes in structured form.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a parser for Portfolio /program and /eloadok pages and FinTechZone /program pages that extracts (session title, speaker, role, organisation) tuples, then flags sessions containing both a bank and a non-bank organisation as candidate partnership disclosures.

coverage_gaps.description: Foreign branches (fióktelep) and cross-border service providers were not systematically explored; a foreign payments vendor may serve HU banks with no Hungarian Kft. at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated sweep for 'fióktelep' and 'kereskedelmi képviselet' registrations, and use BRIS 'Find a company' plus MNB/EBA cross-border notification lists to catch entity-less market presence.

coverage_gaps.description: No TEÁOR/NACE-code-driven screen of the full HU supplier population was executed — only name-based lookups of known vendors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define the target TEÁOR'25 code set (e.g. 6201/6202/6209/6311/4651/6612/6619), then obtain a code-filtered company list via Opten Cégtár, D&B, or a licensed Céginformációs Szolgálat extract to discover unknown challengers.

coverage_gaps.description: Other Hungarian credit/company-information houses (e.g. Crefoport, Coface Hungary, Creditreform, EMIS/CEIC-type regional databases) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up hu+en sweep on 'cégminősítés', 'hitelinformáció', 'credit report Hungary' to complete the commercial-provider inventory and compare pricing/coverage before subscribing.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical ownership change tracking (who bought which HU vendor, when) was identified conceptually via cégtörténet and Cégközlöny archives, but no archive depth/retention limits were established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test how far back Cégközlöny issue archives and Opten cégtörténet reach, and record retention limits so historical M&A reconstruction is scoped realistically.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature — the statutory portals and filings are Hungarian-only, and English guides found were mostly commercial company-formation marketing of low evidential value.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for Hungarian-language parsing (mérleg/eredménykimutatás line-item vocabulary) in the collection pipeline; use the EU e-Justice HU page as the only reliable English reference layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Healthcare buyers (hospitals, clinics, ÁEEK/OKFŐ-managed institutions) are entirely uncovered for kiosks, patient check-in terminals and payment automats.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted EKR/Közbeszerzési Értesítő searches on betegirányító rendszer, kioszk, fizetőautomata, parkolás with healthcare contracting authorities; add OKFŐ and large hospitals to the actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: Utilities (MVM Next, regional víziközmű and távhő providers) and their customer-service payment points are not represented among the sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search hu for MVM ügyfélszolgálat befizetés automata, csekkbefizető automata, sárga csekk automata; check MVM procurement/transparency pages and EKR.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level procurement (TED - Tenders Electronic Daily) was not searched, although the largest HU automat/kiosk contracts are above threshold and are published there in both hu and en with structured CPV data.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add TED (ted.europa.eu) as a structured, API-accessible source filtered to country=HU with CPV families for vending machines, ticket-issuing machines, POS terminals and cash-handling equipment.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only vendor-global material (NCR/Diebold Nixdorf corporate) surfaced, with no en-language HU market analysis.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add en searches on 'Hungary self-checkout market', 'Hungary unattended payment kiosk rollout', RBR/Datos and Retail Banking Research style reports, plus vendor EN press rooms filtered for Hungary.

coverage_gaps.description: Supplier attribution for private retail chains is missing across the board; sources give installed base but not who supplied it.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Triangulate via Hungarian company filings (e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu) of vendor subsidiaries, integrator reference pages, NAV e-pénztárgép licence holders, and job postings mentioning specific SCO platforms.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-handling specifics (cash recycling, CIT, smart safes) for retail and fuel buyers are not represented; only card and ticketing evidence was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search hu on készpénzkezelés kiskereskedelem, pénzkezelő automata, készpénzlogisztika, and monitor MNB cash-cycle publications for retail cash-handling policy affecting these buyers.

coverage_gaps.description: Támogatásokat Vizsgáló Iroda (TVI, the Hungarian state aid monitoring office at the Ministry of Finance) and any national de minimis / aid register were not searched in this pass.
